description: One column of `<c>` elements whose `t` names a type but whose payload is missing or empty: every `t` with no `<v>`, an empty `<v>` under b/s/e/d, a self-closing `<v/>`, an inlineStr carrying a `<v>` and no `<is>`, a whitespace-only pool index, and the string types with their carrier present but empty. A20 (`t="b"` `<v>0</v>`) and A21 (`t="s"` `<v>0</v>`) are controls. The package is hand-built, because the writer never emits these shapes, so it was observed directly rather than emitted from a probe spec.
readback: Range.Value2 type, Range.Text, and Worksheet.Evaluate of ISBLANK/TYPE/COUNTA per cell; UsedRange.Address
resave: Observed on an earlier package of the same shapes: Excel's SaveAs dropped every blank cell from `<sheetData>` and wrote each empty-text cell as a pooled empty string (`<c t="s"><v>0</v></c>` over `<si><t/></si>`).
malformedTokens: Observed in separate packages, one cell each: `t="s"` with `<v>abc</v>`, `t="s"` with an index past the pool, `t="b"` with `<v>2</v>`, and `t="e"` with `<v>junk</v>` all make Workbooks.Open throw (a package Excel refuses without repair).
verdict: A cell Excel shows as blank carries no value, whatever its `t`. The string types are text once their carrier is present, empty or self-closing, and blank without it; every other type is blank unless its `<v>` holds a token, an empty `<v>` reading the same as a missing one. An inlineStr ignores `<v>`. The readers match: blank shapes read as null and are not streamed, carrier-present string cells read as the empty string.
